claims.statement: Treat survival and board presence as Winnu's opening priority: its starting fleet is too small to expand and defend comfortably, so it needs more units before pursuing ambitious plays.
claims.conditions: Especially in round one and when neighbors can reach the home system or first expansion; the guide describes elimination risk as unusually high.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current rules and later changes not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Starting force details are spoken quickly; advice is the hosts' assessment, not a universal matchup rule.

claims.statement: Use Dark Energy Tap as the usual starting technology when choosing the non-prerequisite starting tech; the guide values starting on the blue path and calls DET a useful source of options.
claims.conditions: A default, not a rule: later technology access depends on the table, slice, and Winnu's need to spend resources on units.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current rules and later changes not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Podcast preference; the transcript's faction name and tech explanations contain ASR errors.

claims.statement: Expect a thin early economy: the guide describes a single 3-resource/4-influence home planet and three commodities, leaving little cash for both technology and defense.
claims.conditions: Use the resource constraint when weighing round-one scoring, technology, and unit production; trade goods or a favorable slice can change the choice.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); planet values and current rules not independently checked.
claims.uncertainty: The transcript contains a noisy aside about commodities; the three-commodity figure is clearly stated later in the faction overview.

claims.statement: Do not build a round-one plan around taking Mecatol Rex for Custodians: the hosts argue that Winnu's discount is rarely decisive, while the required tech and exposed slice can leave it easy to attack.
claims.conditions: This is their default risk judgment, particularly when taking the point requires diverting scarce resources from plastic; map, draft, and table behavior matter.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts report their observed games rather than establish that early Custodians can never work.

claims.statement: Blood Ties waives spending influence to remove the Custodians token, but the guide treats it as a one-time effect that often goes unused and says six influence is usually attainable anyway.
claims.conditions: Relevant only if Winnu takes Mecatol Rex for the Custodians point; do not overvalue the ability when evaluating ordinary economy.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Podcast opinion on how hard six influence is to obtain is table dependent.

claims.statement: Reclamation places a PDS and space dock on Mecatol Rex after the tactical action that captures it; because the ability resolves after production, those structures do not produce during that action.
claims.conditions: Only applies when Winnu gains control of Mecatol Rex through a tactical action and has the structures in reinforcements.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); rules timing is reported by the hosts and not independently rules-checked.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers call it a rare, potentially once-per-game opportunity.

claims.statement: The Reclaimer mech can place a PDS or space dock on a planet it captures; multiple mechs capturing together can place several structures, which can help with structure objectives and reduce dependence on Construction.
claims.conditions: Build and move the mechs to the relevant planet, and account for the delayed payoff: the discussion says these structures arrive after production and cannot build units immediately that turn.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers say Winnu almost always takes its mech and describe the structure-objective application as situational.

claims.statement: The agent reduces the combined cost of units produced by two; the hosts value it mainly as round-one help getting needed plastic onto the board, roughly two trade goods of relief when used.
claims.conditions: Use when resolving production and when the reduction affects units you actually need; later uses remain useful but are less transformative than fixing the opening.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The two-trade-good valuation and round-one emphasis are strategic estimates from the hosts.

claims.statement: The commander gives Winnu +2 to combat rolls in its home system, Mecatol Rex, and systems with legendary planets; the hosts chiefly value this as help holding home and a contested Mecatol.
claims.conditions: It must first be unlocked by controlling Mecatol Rex or entering combat in its system; outside the listed locations it provides no protection.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts call the control-Mecatol unlock oddly worded and emphasize that bonus combat results do little for a very small fleet.

claims.statement: Do not count on the flagship as a stand-alone answer: its dice scale with opposing non-fighter ships, so a heavy fighter screen can leave it rolling very little; the hosts say the commander makes it more relevant.
claims.conditions: Most relevant when deciding whether to spend eight resources and when judging a fleet with commander support; fighters in the opposing fleet blunt its special scaling.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current unit statistics not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The transcript mangles the flagship's name; the component reference identifies it as Salai Sai Corian.

claims.statement: The guide is sharply negative on both faction technologies: Lazax Gate Folding's wormhole access matters only while Winnu lacks Mecatol, while its infantry action matters only after Winnu controls it; Hegemonic Trade Policy is called too narrow to justify its technology detour.
claims.conditions: These evaluations concern opportunity cost in a game where the guide prioritizes plastic and blue technology; Hegemonic Trade Policy has a niche production-step use on Mecatol Rex.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current technology text not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts' negative valuation is strategic opinion; exact card wording and edition status need rules verification.

claims.statement: Acquiescence lets its recipient resolve a strategy card's secondary without spending or placing a command token; the guide prices it modestly and finds its cleanest value in a round-one Diplomacy deal that frees Winnu for a third action.
claims.conditions: Sell or trade it when the recipient values the saved token and timing; Leadership costs no token for its secondary, and some strategy-card secondaries make the note less valuable.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); the described note is its Omega version; current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers value it around one trade good and present Construction as a possible interaction, while noting that the player usually must already activate the system to place the structure.

claims.statement: Mathis Mathinus's hero performs the primary of any strategy card, then lets any number of other players perform its secondary before it is purged; the guide treats it as Winnu's decisive catch-up tool.
claims.conditions: The action is a component ability rather than a strategic action; the discussion explicitly says Acquiescence does not apply and Coup d'Etat cannot cancel it.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The transcript varies the hero's spoken name; component-reference.json resolves it to Mathis Mathinus.

claims.statement: The usual hero swing is Imperial: catch up through a public point, and when conditions allow, combine the Mecatol Rex Custodians point with Imperial scoring; non-Imperial hero uses are described as narrow-window exceptions.
claims.conditions: Depends on the public objective, Mecatol access, Imperial timing, and the players' secondaries; it can invite immediate table retaliation.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); scoring requirements and current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts describe this as the common pattern, not an automatic two-point result or guaranteed safe line.

claims.statement: The guide's central diagnosis is that Winnu's late tempo is strong but its people problem is surviving opponents: if Winnu stays alive through rounds one and two, its controllable hero timing can bring it back into contention.
claims.conditions: The guide's plan assumes the table does not eliminate or cripple Winnu before its round-five hero; survival and table diplomacy are more important than keeping pace early.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); guide meta snapshot, not current win-rate evidence.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts acknowledge Winnu results are hard to judge because memorable wins may distort perception of frequent losses.

claims.statement: Avoid stretching the weak opening to score merely for round-one tempo; the guide argues that an early point can make Winnu look ahead while its fleet remains easy to attack, and the hero offers a later catch-up path.
claims.conditions: If an objective is naturally reachable without exposing the slice or sacrificing defense, the guide does not forbid scoring it; its warning is about forced, costly scoring.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); guide advice, current objective deck not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The assessment depends on table threat perception and objective availability.

claims.statement: Treat Leadership as low priority because it does not directly build the fleet; consider it as a late pick when Diplomacy and Warfare are taken and favorable secondaries make the tokens useful.
claims.conditions: The speakers describe this as a conditional draft choice, not a ban on taking Leadership; timing and the remaining secondaries matter.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); strategy card timing not independently reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: Draft order examples are conversational and table dependent.

claims.statement: Diplomacy can be a useful money pick, but its return depends on the slice and whether Trade was taken; Winnu's three-resource home limits its default value.
claims.conditions: When choosing Diplomacy in round one, offer Acquiescence to a player who values its secondary timing, especially if that helps coordinate later Warfare or Technology actions.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The guide calls the card decent while recognizing it can enrich opponents more than Winnu on an influence-rich map.

claims.statement: Construction is usually a poor Winnu pick because the mech supplies structures; consider it chiefly when a structure objective makes the clean round-one structure placement valuable.
claims.conditions: The guide's example is building a mech and using its capture ability to produce a third structure outside the home system; the agent helps fund that mech.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current objective and rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers say other plans can also meet structure objectives, so Construction is convenient rather than necessary.

claims.statement: Warfare is a round-one survival priority: the guide says Winnu may need to take it itself at a late draft position if no one else appears likely to, because otherwise its expansion and fleet position can stall.
claims.conditions: This is strongest when the table seems unlikely to select Warfare; coordinate with Diplomacy only if timing works, and sell Acquiescence when another player values the Warfare secondary.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The hosts acknowledge player exceptions but attribute successful aggressive exceptions to unusually passive opponents.

claims.statement: Technology is attractive when its primary grants the needed tech without spending Winnu's scarce resources, but the recommended line is DET, Gravity Drive, Carrier II, then stop and prioritize units.
claims.conditions: Use Gravity Drive when it improves reach to valuable systems; Technology secondaries are for the exceptional case where production is already capped and about four trade goods remain.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current technology prerequisites and rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: This is a default path, not a claim that further technology is never useful; the hosts expressly allow slice-specific tech needs.

claims.statement: The guide's preferred defense is enough plastic to make Winnu inconvenient to attack; it names Carrier II with many fighters as cost-effective and compatible with the commander's combat bonus.
claims.conditions: Spend on ships and screens before optional technology when the economy is tight; a forward production base can help, but structures placed by the mech do not build immediately on the capture turn.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current rules and unit costs not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The guide presents this as deterrence and survival, not proof that a fleet wins a direct fight or a guarantee against attack.

claims.statement: Spend available income on plastic rather than influence by default: the guide says Winnu often skips costly secondaries and can use the hero instead of farming one more secret-objective draw late.
claims.conditions: Keep enough command tokens for the actions actually planned; resource-rich slices are especially valuable, and the hosts cite an influence-heavy planet as useful because its income could be converted to units.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); advice about objective timing and current rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The guide's winning-game example is anecdotal; slice and token needs vary.

claims.statement: The Alliance can protect its buyer's home and may be worth trading, but avoid giving it to a player who also expects to fight over Mecatol Rex: their borrowed +2 can work against Winnu there.
claims.conditions: If Mecatol is not a likely contest, the hosts suggest selling the note for more plastic or trading it to a partner who values late-game protection.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current promissory-note rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The transcript calls this Winnu's Alliance; component-reference lists the Winnu alliance note as promissory:<color>_an.

claims.statement: Prepare by round four for a round-five hero swing; one suggested sequence is to take Mecatol Rex on the last action of round four so Imperial can score early in round five.
claims.conditions: This can improve action-phase timing or status-phase initiative, depending on the setup and the other factions; taking Mecatol early also makes Winnu the table's obvious focus.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); objective, initiative, and rules interactions not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The guide calls full round-four setup demanding and labels the Mecatol sequence clever but risky.

claims.statement: The late hero is powerful but conditional: favorable stage-two objectives may let Winnu vault forward, while the same threat can prompt the table to eliminate it; the guide's mitigation is to remain hard to stop early and avoid looking far ahead.
claims.conditions: Assess revealed objectives, fleet position, and opponents' ability to reach Winnu before choosing whether to accelerate.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); guide-era meta snapshot.
claims.uncertainty: The guide gives no reliable defense against a coordinated table and explicitly says winning is not easy.

claims.statement: Do not mistake the recommended Carrier II and Gravity Drive path, even with Light/Wave later, for a reliable win-slay package; the hosts say Winnu should survive quietly and rely on leaders ahead of it to stop each other.
claims.conditions: This is the guide's late-game limitation when others race ahead; the plan seeks relevance and a narrow catch-up win, not the ability to remove a leader from contention.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); current unit and technology rules not reviewed.
claims.uncertainty: The speakers distinguish blocking a point or taking a system from what they call a full slay; their assessment is not a tested matchup result.

claims.statement: The guide's practical success pattern is a quiet early game with enough units to deter attacks, followed by the hero's late catch-up; it reports recent tournament and async wins that coasted instead of forcing early Custodians or tempo.
claims.conditions: Treat these anecdotes as support for the low-profile approach, not as a guarantee; the authors also say a Winnu game can simply fail if the table acts against it.
claims.compatibility: SCPT 352 (2024-05-22); anecdotes and contemporary meta only.
claims.uncertainty: Named tournament/game descriptions are brief and partly ASR-distorted; no game records are cited.

connections.conditions: The agent's production discount can help afford an early mech when Winnu needs to place plastic or pursue a structure objective.

The commander adds combat strength in its listed systems, while a large fleet gives that bonus more opportunities to matter; the hosts specifically say fighters can become threatening with the bonus and action cards.
The guide's stated blue path combines Gravity Drive with Carrier II to improve carrier reach for late-game positioning; it does not claim this pair alone can slay a leader.
The hero can resolve Imperial's primary as a late catch-up action when the objective and Mecatol timing support scoring; the use may trigger a table response.
Giving Alliance to a Mecatol rival can let that player use Winnu's combat bonus against Winnu in the Mecatol Rex system.
The speakers say opposing heavy fighter screens reduce the Winnu flagship's dice because its dice count opposing non-fighter ships.
